case_name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
holding: Established the 'Basic Structure Doctrine', holding that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure or essential features of the Constitution.

case_name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
holding: Expanded Article 21 right to life and personal liberty to mandate that procedure established by law must be just, fair, and reasonable, incorporating due process.

case_name: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu
holding: Formulated the new doctrine of equality under Article 14, holding that equality is a dynamic concept opposed to arbitrariness.

case_name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
holding: Unanimously affirmed the Right to Privacy as a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution.

case_name: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
holding: Initial narrow interpretation of Article 21 restricting 'procedure established by law' strictly to enacted statutory procedure (later overruled by Maneka Gandhi).

case_name: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
holding: Held that right to education up to age 14 is a fundamental right flowing directly from Article 21, paving the way for Article 21A.

case_name: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
holding: Upheld constitutional validity of Right to Education Act 2009 under Article 21A, mandating 25% reservation for underprivileged children in private schools.

case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
holding: Struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act as unconstitutional under Article 19(1)(a) for overbreadth and restricting free speech.

case_name: Bennett Coleman & Co. v. Union of India
holding: Affirmed that freedom of the press is an integral part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

case_name: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
holding: Upheld Jehovah's Witnesses students' right to refrain from singing the National Anthem under Article 19(1)(a) and Article 25 freedom of conscience.

case_name: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala (Sabarimala Case)
holding: Held that excluding women aged 10-50 from Sabarimala temple violated Articles 14, 15, 21, and 25, ruling religious customs subject to constitutional morality.

case_name: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
holding: Held judicial review under Article 32 and Article 226 as part of basic structure, making decisions of tribunals subject to High Court jurisdiction.

case_name: Prem Chand Garg v. Supreme Court of India
holding: Rule that right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 for enforcement of Fundamental Rights is itself a fundamental right.

case_name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
holding: Curbed arbitrary misuse of President's Rule under Article 356, establishing that proclamation is subject to judicial review and federalism is basic structure.

case_name: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
holding: Struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 inserted by 42nd Amendment, reiterating that Parliament's amending power is limited.

case_name: In re Article 370 of the Constitution
holding: Unanimously upheld the constitutional validity of C.O. 272 and C.O. 273 abrogating special status under Article 370 and reorganizing Jammu and Kashmir.
Held that Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, though unenforceable directly, must be used to interpret constitutional provisions and statutes.
